title: Sprint-slot auction and scope fractionation guidelines
creator: Maya Patel
description: Introduce an operational pattern for allocating fixed sprint capacity across competing initiatives using a lightweight internal auction ("Focus Credits") plus a formalized scope fractionation checklist. Goal: reduce ad-hoc zero-sum fights mid-cycle, surface trade-offs, and increase predictability for staffing and handoffs. The outcome is a repeatable process Product Managers and Eng Leads use at start-of-cycle and for mid-cycle rebalancing. This ticket captures policy, minimum tooling needs, acceptance criteria, and a rollout plan for a pilot across two initiatives (Console observability and Dedicated autoscaling).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Run a pilot auction for Q2-W1 across 3 teams with documented bids and final allocation decisions.
A2: Provide a fractionation checklist template that decomposes feature work into <=3 micro-slices with independent acceptance criteria and measurable value signals.
A3: Create a simple spreadsheet + Confluence form to record Focus Credit budgets, bids, and rationale; link to cycle dashboard.
A4: Post-pilot retrospective with quantitative metrics: % of committed work completed, number of mid-cycle scope rescues, and lead time variance pre/post pilot.
A5: Engineering confirms estimated ramp/overhead < 3% of sprint capacity for auction coordination (instrumentation & meetings).
A6: Playbook approved by PM lead and Eng manager, with sign-off comments in Confluence.
A7: Documented fallback rules for urgent SEV work that must preempt auctioned slots.
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Decided to use Focus Credits (non-transferable) allocated by OKR weight + initiative risk factor rather than dollar-based bidding to avoid gaming.
2026-03-02: Agreed auction cadence = weekly lead-up to cycle lock (2-week window), then ad-hoc micro-auctions for leftover capacity.
2026-03-05: Trade-off: keep auction lightweight (spreadsheet + form) vs building an automated tool. Decided pilot manual; tool backlog if pilot shows >=3 auctions/month.
2026-03-10: Added explicit guardrails for cross-team dependencies: any bid that requires >1 team must include a cross-team dependency owner and a shadow slot owner.
2026-03-12: Approved fractionation checklist; added requirement that each micro-slice must be demonstrable in isolation (end-to-end smoke) and have a rollback plan.
comments: 2026-02-26 - Maya Patel: Initial proposal shared with PM council. Rationale: recurring capacity fights and late-cycle scope churn are increasing OKR slippage. See draft playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CYC/Sprint+Slot+Auction+Draft

2026-03-01 - Ethan Brooks: Pushed back on auction complexity for small teams. Suggested a minimum-viable variant: 'slot-reservation' where teams request slots and PMs adjudicate using credit signals. Decided to keep auction for pilot but include reservation fallback.
2026-03-03 - Priya Singh (Eng Manager): Engineering flagged instrumentation needed to measure freed-up KV-cache tuning work. Tagged ENG-20421 for dashboarding and ENG-20422 for dependency mapping.

2026-03-06 - Ben Ortiz (Design): Recommended adding a stakeholder communication template for scope cuts to preserve customer-facing messaging and avoid surprise UX regressions. Draft attached: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folder/0B_demo/scope-cut-templates
2026-03-08 - Claire Xu (PM Lead): Approved pilot cohort: Console Observability (PM: K. Morales) and Dedicated Autoscaling (PM: J. Park). Requested outcome metrics and a retrospective date.

2026-03-11 - Engineering review: Confirmed overhead estimate ~2% of sprint capacity for coordination; flagged risk of cross-team split stories increasing merge conflicts. Action: require a 'shadow owner' and daily sync during implementation weeks.

2026-03-12 - Maya Patel: Uploaded final fractionation checklist and sample bid spreadsheet to Confluence. Next: schedule pilot kickoff and stakeholder training (30 minutes). Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CYC/Sprint+Slot+Auction+Pilot
rollout_plan: Step 1: Pilot in 2026-W11 with two initiatives; run auction and fractionation at T-10 days to sprint lock.
Step 2: Capture metrics during pilot; weekly check-ins with Eng leads and PMs for 3 sprints.
Step 3: Retro + decision (continue, refine, stop) after pilot; if continue, schedule tooling ticket (ENG backlog) for lightweight web form.
Step 4: If adopted, incorporate auction cadence into cycle onboarding and PM training docs.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Auction overhead steals execution time -> Mitigation: pilot manual, cap coordination time to 2 hours/week per PM, measure overhead.
Risk: Gaming bids to protect vanity projects -> Mitigation: allocate Focus Credits by OKR weight and require written rationale; PM council review for anomalous bids.
Risk: Cross-team story fragmentation increases technical debt -> Mitigation: require fractionation checklist and shadow owner, limit splits to <=3 micro-slices with CI gates.
